title: Boss: Sensor Pi
intro: The Sensor Pi never fights the same way twice: every arena has its own rhythm, so counting won't save you. Luckily its antenna glows before each strike. [b]boss_charging()[/b] is true when the boss in front of you will strike on the next turn, and [b]boss_ahead()[/b] is true while a boss is still standing in front of you.
cs_note: Hard-coding works only for the input you've already seen. A program that [b]reads the situation[/b] each turn (if it's charging, block; otherwise attack) handles any rhythm, including ones nobody has shown you yet.
hints: Look at the three arena tabs: each boss strikes on a different beat.
Every turn, ask one question: is it about to strike? If so block(), otherwise attack().

Wrap an if … else in [b]while boss_ahead()[/b]: if boss_charging(), block(); else attack(). The while keeps fighting until the boss falls, however long that takes, and the if picks the right move for each turn of whatever rhythm this arena has.
